'''Sviatoslav Ivanovych "Slava" Vakarchuk''' ({{langx|uk|Святослав Іванович "Слава" Вакарчук}}; born 14 May 1975) is a Ukrainian musician, politician, public activist, and soldier. He is the lead vocalist of [[Okean Elzy]], a [[rock music|rock]] band in Ukraine. Vakarchuk is a former<ref name="pravda7257275">[https://www.pravda.com.ua/news/2020/06/26/7257275/ "Voice" took away Vakarchuk's deputy mandate], [[Ukrayinska Pravda]] (26 June 2020) {{in lang|uk}}</ref> [[People's Deputy of Ukraine]],<ref>{{Cite web |title=Офіційний портал Верховної Ради України |url=https://itd.rada.gov.ua/mps/info/page/11120 |access-date=2025-10-31 |website=itd.rada.gov.ua}}</ref><ref name="Verkhovna Rada Deputies List">{{Cite web|url=https://itd.rada.gov.ua/radatransl/Home/deps/en|title=Verkhovna Rada Deputies List}}</ref> and the founder of the [[Voice (Ukrainian political party)|Voice]] (in May 2019).<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.pravda.com.ua/news/2019/05/16/7215170|script-title=uk:Вакарчук заявив про створення партії і похід у Раду|website=pravda.com.ua|language=uk|accessdate=16 May 2019}}</ref>

Vakarchuk was active in supporting the [[Orange Revolution]] and [[Euromaidan]], and is involved in many social and cultural projects. He is one of the most successful musicians in Ukraine and has a PhD degree in [[theoretical physics]].

Vakarchuk is the son of [[Ivan Vakarchuk]], a professor of physics at [[Lviv University]] and a former Ukrainian  [[Ministry of Education and Science of Ukraine|Minister of Education and Science]].

==Biography==

===Musical career===

Vakarchuk was born in the western Ukrainian city of [[Mukachevo]], into a family of scientists.<ref name="vakarchuk201891">[https://www.nytimes.com/2018/09/14/world/europe/ukraine-rock-star-vakarchuk.html?rref=collection%2Fbyline%2Fandrew-e.-kramer For His Next Act, a Ukrainian Rock Star Looks to Politics], [[The New York Times]] (14 September 2018)</ref> His mother and father were both university professors of physics.<ref name="vakarchuk201891"/> His father [[Ivan Vakarchuk]] (1947-2020) served as Ukraine's [[Ministry of Education and Science of Ukraine|Education Minister]].<ref name="vakarchuk-to-study-at-yale-as-third">
[https://www.kyivpost.com/article/content/business/vakarchuk-to-study-at-yale-as-third-ukrainian-fellow-386989.html Vakarchuk to study at Yale as third Ukrainian fellow], [[Kyiv Post]] (23 April 2015)</ref><ref name="10945319Vakarchuk">[https://www.unian.ua/m/society/10945319-pomer-kolishniy-rektor-lvivskogo-universitetu-ivan-vakarchuk.html Former Rector of Lviv University Ivan Vakarchuk died], [[UNIAN]] (4 March 2020) {{in lang|uk}}</ref>

Vakarchuk founded the band [[Okean Elzy]] ("Ocean of Elza"), in 1994 as an undergraduate at [[Lviv University]].<ref name="vakarchuk201891"/> At this university he earned a Ph.D. in the field of [[supersymmetry]].<ref name="vakarchuk201891"/> After graduating Vakarchuk moved to [[Kyiv]].<ref name="vakarchuk201891"/>

In 2005, Vakarchuk answered all questions correctly and won the grand prize ([[Ukrainian hryvnia|₴]]1 million) for the first time on the Ukrainian version of [[Who Wants to Be a Millionaire?]], called [[Khto khoche staty milyonerom? – Pershyi milyon]]. He donated his winnings to orphanages in Ukraine.<ref>[http://vakarchuk.com/novyny/2005/02/02/vakarchuk-trishky-pobuv-milyonerom/ ''Вакарчук трішки побув мільйонером'']</ref>

In support of their album "Zemlya" in spring 2013, the band embarked on a stadium tour throughout cities in Ukraine, Russia, Belarus, the US, Canada, and a number of countries in Western Europe.

In December 2013, Okean Elzy performed during the [[Euromaidan]] protests.<ref>[http://zeenews.india.com/news/world/ukraine-suspends-mayor-security-official-over-protest-crackdown_896844.html Ukraine suspends mayor, security official over protest crackdown], [[Zee News]] (14 December 2013)</ref>

In the summer of 2014, Okean Elzy performed a number of large concerts in the biggest stadiums in Ukraine to mark the band's 20th anniversary. Their performance in Kyiv's [[Olympic Stadium (Kyiv)|Olympic Stadium]] broke the record for the largest number of people attending a concert by a Ukrainian band — over 75,000.

In 2024, Okean Elzy released two albums in the same year, and to celebrate went on tour in Europe and the US. During this tour, which coincided with the band's 30th anniversary and included new cities it had previously not played at, Okean Elzy raised funds for Ukraine.

===Political career===

In the early [[2007 Ukrainian parliamentary election|30 September 2007 parliamentary election]], he ran as an independent candidate on the [[Our Ukraine–People's Self-Defense Bloc]]'s list (as No. 15). In the [[Verkhovna Rada]] (Ukrainian parliament) he was a member of the parliamentary committee for [[freedom of speech]] issues. He was also a member of groups of parliamentary contacts with the [[Russia|Russian Federation]] and other countries.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://itd.rada.gov.ua/mps/info/expage/11120/7|title=Офіційний портал Верховної Ради України|website=itd.rada.gov.ua|access-date=6 April 2018}}</ref> Vakarchuk did not submit any legislative acts during his deputy's term. He submitted two amendments, one of which was accepted by the Verkhovna Rada.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://w1.c1.rada.gov.ua/pls/pt2/reports.dep2?PERSON=11120&SKL=7|title=Офіційний портал Верховної Ради України|website=w1.c1.rada.gov.ua|access-date=6 April 2018}}</ref> In early September 2008, he renounced his seat in the Verkhovna Rada due to the [[2008 Ukrainian political crisis|political situation]].<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.gazeta.ru/news/lenta/2008/09/11/n_1269306.shtml|title=Солист "Океана Эльзы" отказался от депутатского мандата|date=11 September 2008|accessdate=11 September 2008|publisher=[[Gazeta.ru]]}} 
</ref> On 16 December 2008, the Verkhovna Rada accepted Vakarchuk's renunciation.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://zakon.rada.gov.ua/go/664-17|title=Про дострокове припинення повноважень народного депутата У... {{!}} від 16 December 2008 № 664-VI|website=zakon.rada.gov.ua|access-date=6 April 2018}}</ref> According to Vakarchuk, he renounced his seat because “I was really frustrated by the level of mutual fights, at the absurd [[Hobbesian]] world of all against all, rather than changing the country for the better.”<ref name="vakarchuk201891"/>
[[file:Вакарчук, Харьков.jpg|thumb|Svyatoslav Vakarchuk in [[Kharkiv]], <br />[[Ukraine]] on 19 April 2008]]
In 2008, Vakarchuk released a solo project "[[Vnochi (music album)|Vnochi]]" (In the Night). This album was released under the name of Svyatoslav Vakarchuk, but it includes appearances by all members of [[Okean Elzy]] and other various guest musicians. Another solo project followed in 2011, "[[Brussel (music album)|Brussel]]" (Brussels).

In 2015, Vakarchuk took part in the [[Yale World Fellows]] international fellowship program at [[Yale University]].<ref name="vakarchuk-to-study-at-yale-as-third"/>

Vakarchuk stated multiple times in 2017 that he had no political ambitions.<ref>[http://m.expres.ua/#!/n/259102 President Vakarchuk: The musician spoke about political ambitions], [[Ekspres]] (26 August 2017) {{in lang|uk}}<br />[http://www.pravda.com.ua/news/2017/12/10/7165015/ Vakarchuk broke away from political ambitions, but called 10 points for Ukraine's development], [[Ukrayinska Pravda]] (10 December 2017) {{in lang|uk}}</ref> However, in 2018 he joined [[Stanford University]] as a visiting scholar,<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.okeanelzy.com/en/news/437/|title=Sviatoslav Vakarchuk joins Stanford as a visiting scholar this fall|website=www.okeanelzy.com|access-date=18 September 2018}}</ref> focusing on politics and leadership. Later that year he appeared at several politically themed conferences, speaking alongside established Ukrainian politicians.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://yes-ukraine.org/en/news/vladu-v-ukrayini-mayut-vzyati-lyudi-yakim-doviryaye-suspilstvo-svyatoslav-vakarchuk|title=Vakarchuk presents at Yalta YES conference|website=yes-ukraine.org|access-date=18 September 2018}}</ref> This led the public to view him as a potential candidate for the [[2019 Ukrainian presidential election]], where he became one of the frontrunners according to [[Opinion polling for the Ukrainian presidential election, 2019|opinion polls]]. But by late 2018 he was overtaken by other potential candidates, and in October 2018 he stated “Who can change the political culture is more important than who becomes the president.”<ref>[https://www.kyivpost.com/ukraine-politics/5-months-before-voting-race-for-president-well-under-way.html 5 months before voting, race for president well under way] (2 November 2018)</ref>{{Efn|In January 2019, ''[[Ukrainska Pravda]]'' commented that Vakarchuk was not going to go to take part in the [[2019 Ukrainian presidential election]] but that his likely goal was to participate in [[2019 Ukrainian parliamentary election|parliamentary elections]].<ref>[https://www.pravda.com.ua/news/2019/01/23/7204652/ Vakarchuk about the election: I'm in action], [[Ukrayinska Pravda]] (23 January 2019) {{in lang|uk}}</ref>}} In the election Vakarchuk did not back any of the candidates.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://en.interfax.com.ua/news/general/562024.html|title=Musician Vakarchuk says he doesn't plan to back any Ukrainian presidential candidate|website=en.interfax.com.ua|access-date=24 March 2019}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://ua.interfax.com.ua/news/election2019/574720.html|title=Гриценко вважає, що Вакарчук має публічно висловити свою позицію на цих виборах|website=ua.interfax.com.ua|language=uk|access-date=24 March 2019}}</ref> According to an early March 2019 poll by [[sociological group "RATING"]], 64% of the electorate would have liked to see Vakarchuk among the presidential candidates.<ref>{{in lang|uk}} [https://www.pravda.com.ua/news/2019/03/11/7208853/ 20% of Ukrainians would like Vakarchuk to go to the presidency], [[Ukrayinska Pravda]] (11 March 2019)</ref>

Vakarchuk also plays an active role in social and cultural projects, and is the founder of the charity foundation "Lyudi Maybutnyoho" (People of the Future). The main projects of the foundation were "Knyga Tvoryt' Lyudynu" (A Book Creates a Man), "Osvita Krainoyu" (The Country's Education), "3-D Proekt. Dumay, Diy, Dopomagai." (3-D Project. Think, Act. Help.). Together with the members of the band he actively supported the preventive campaign IOM and MTV Europe's "People Are Not For Sale." In 2003, Vakarchuk became an Honorary Ambassador of Culture in Ukraine. In 2005, he became a Goodwill Ambassador for the United Nations Development Programme.

On 16 May 2019, Vakarchuk announced the creation of a new political party, [[Holos (political party)|Holos]] (Voice or Vote), with  the aim to participate in the [[2019 Ukrainian parliamentary election|July 2019 parliamentary election]].<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.rferl.org/a/ukraine-rock-star-vakarchuk-political-party-general-elections/29944421.html|title=Rock Star Vakarchuk Sets Up Political Party Ahead Of Ukraine's General Elections|newspaper=Radio Free Europe/Radio Liberty|date=16 May 2019 |language=en|access-date=16 May 2019}}</ref> Vakarchuk assured on 19 May 2019 that if elected to parliament, he would not stop playing music, but political activity would be a priority.<ref name="7215497/ Vakarchuk">{{in lang|uk}} [https://www.pravda.com.ua/news/2019/05/19/7215497/ Vakarchuk: There will be no acting deputies in the list of new party], Ukrayinska Pravda (19 May 2019)</ref> He also claimed that he believed that currently the [[Ukrainian parliament]] is the place "where real changes are being made" so he did not participate in the presidential election of the previous month.<ref name="7215497/ Vakarchuk"/> Vakarchuk was elected to the Verkhovna Rada in July 2019.<ref name="Verkhovna Rada Deputies List"/> His party gained 5.82% of the vote.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.cvk.gov.ua/pls/vnd2019/wp300pt001f01=919.html|title=Центральна виборча комісія - Вибори народних депутатів України 2019|website=www.cvk.gov.ua|access-date=2 October 2019}}</ref> On 11 June 2020 Vakarchuk registered in parliament a request to terminate his parliamentary mandate.<ref name=668082Vakarchuk/> He insisted that he did not plan to end his political career but would be working on [[extra-parliamentary]] activities for his party.<ref name=668082Vakarchuk>[https://en.interfax.com.ua/news/general/668082.html Vakarchuk resigns as Member of Parliament], [[Interfax-Ukraine]] (11 June 2020)</ref> On 18 June 2020 parliament rejected the draft resolution on the early termination of Vakarchuk's parliamentary mandate (the resolution was supported by 175 deputies, while 226 votes minimum were required).<ref name="3047786vakarchuks">[https://www.ukrinform.net/rubric-polytics/3047786-parliament-rejects-vakarchuks-resignation.html Parliament rejects Vakarchuk’s resignation], [[Ukrinform]] (18 June 2020)</ref> The next day Vakarchuk left his party's faction so [[Imperative mandate (Ukraine)|the party could terminate his mandate via a party congress]].<ref name="7256331Vakarchuk">{{in lang|uk}} [https://www.pravda.com.ua/news/2020/06/19/7256331/ Vakarchuk figured out how to get rid of the mandate if the Rada does not release], [[Ukrayinska Pravda]] (19 June 2020)</ref> His party 
did indeed do this on 26 June 2020.<ref name="pravda7257275"/> Vakarchuk was replaced in parliament by [[Andriy Sharaskin]].<ref name="pravda.comSharaskin">{{in lang|uk}} [https://www.pravda.com.ua/news/2020/10/8/7269289/ "Cyborg" Sharaskin will join the Voice Council, Sviderska changed her mind], [[Ukrayinska Pravda]] (8 October 2020)</ref>

===Personal life===

His life partner from the beginning of the 2000s until 2021 was Lialia Fonariova. Together they raised Lialia's daughter from her first marriage with Volodymyr Tarasyuk; she was later adopted by Vakarchuk.[https://showbiz.24tv.ua/istoriya-kohannya-svyatoslava-vakarchuka-novini-shou-biznesu%20n1654920] The couple had no children together.

In June 2021, Vakarchuk announced the end of his relationship with Lialia as a couple,[https://tsn.ua/glamur/svyatoslav-vakarchuk-ogolosiv-pro-rozluchennya-z-kohanoyu-1803481.html]

He is currently in a relationship with Yevheniia Yatsuta. The couple has two children — Ivan (born in 2021) and Solomiya (born in 2022).[https://nv.ua/ukr/life/znamenitosti/svyatoslav-vakarchuk-pokazavsya-na-publici-z-kohanoyu-i-matir-yu-svojih-ditey-yevgeniyeyu-yacutoyu-video-50531237.html]<ref>{{Cite web |last=Sukhachova |first=Tetiana |date=2022-07-05 |title=Святослав Вакарчук став батьком удруге |url=https://tabloid.pravda.com.ua/person/62c44a4bdcb6d/ |access-date=2025-10-05 |website=Ukrainska Pravda |language=uk}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Khmelnytska |first=Vira |date=2022-06-19 |title=Новини шоу-бізнесу: Святослав Вакарчук вперше засвітив однорічного сина |url=https://tsn.ua/glamur/svyatoslav-vakarchuk-vpershe-pokazav-foto-zi-svoyim-odnorichnim-sinom-2090797.html |access-date=2025-10-05 |website=ТSN.ua |language=uk}}</ref>

The Ukrainian magazine ''[[Korrespondent]]'' has ranked him as one of the 100 most influential people in Ukraine (in 2008 ranked 55).<ref>Korrespondent 2008-08-22, nr 32.</ref>

Vakarchuk speaks [[Ukrainian language|Ukrainian]], [[Russian language|Russian]], [[English language|English]] and [[Polish language|Polish]] fluently.

During the [[2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine]], Vakarchuk joined the Ukrainian army.<ref name="Vakarchukterritorial442">[https://kyivindependent.com/uncategorized/musician-svyatoslav-vakarchuk-joins-territorial-defense-unit/ Musician Svyatoslav Vakarchuk joins territorial defense unit], [[The Kyiv Independent]] (7 March 2022)</ref> He joined the [[Territorial defence battalions (Ukraine)|territorial defence battalion]] of [[Lviv Oblast]] on 7 March 2022.<ref name="Vakarchukterritorial442"/>

* [[Merited Artist of Ukraine]] (2005)<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://zakon.rada.gov.ua/laws/show/1193/2005|access-date=10 March 2021|website=zakon.rada.gov.ua|title=Про відзначення державними нагородами України з нагоди 14-ї річниці незалежності України}}</ref>
* [[Vasyl Stus Prize]] (2014)

* Honorary Citizen of [[Kyiv]] (2015)<ref>{{Cite web|date=14 May 2015|title=Вакарчук отримав звання "Почесний громадянин Києва"|url=https://ukranews.com/ua/news/330647-vakarchuk-otrymav-zvannya-pochesnyy-gromadyanyn-kyyeva|access-date=10 March 2021|website=ukranews_com|language=uk}}</ref>
* [[Order of Liberty (Ukraine)|Order of Liberty]] of Ukraine (2016)<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://zakon.rada.gov.ua/laws/show/18/2016|access-date=10 March 2021|website=zakon.rada.gov.ua|title=Про відзначення державними нагородами України з нагоди Дня Соборності України}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|title=Офіційне інтернет-представництво Президента України|url=http://www.president.gov.ua/|access-date=10 March 2021|website=Офіційне інтернет-представництво Президента України|language=uk}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|date=24 January 2016|title=Порошенко нагородив орденами видатних українців на честь Дня Соборності|url=https://ukranews.com/ua/news/405369-poroshenko-nagorodyv-ordenamy-vydatnykh-ukrainciv-na-chest-dnya-sobornosti|access-date=10 March 2021|website=ukranews_com|language=uk}}</ref>

== Discography ==
Vakarchuk has released nine studio albums together with his band, Okean Elzy:

* ''[[Tam, de nas nema]]'' (Where there is no us 1998)
* ''[[Yananebibuv (Okean Elzy album)|Ya na nebi buv]]'' (I was in heaven, 2000)
* ''[[Model (Okean Elzy album)|Model]]'' (2001)
* ''[[Supersymetriya (Okean Elzy album)|Supersymetriya]]'' (Supersymmetry, 2003)
* ''[[Gloria (Okean Elzy album)|GLORIA]]'' (2005)
* ''[[Mira (Okean Elzy album)|Mira]]'' (Measure, 2007)
* ''[[Dolce Vita (Okean Elzy album)|Dolce Vita]]'' (2010)
* ''[[Zemlia (Okean Elzy album)|Zemlia]]'' (Earth, 2013) 
* ''[[Bez mezh (Okean Elzy album)|Bez mezh]]'' (Limitless, 2016)
* ''[[Lighthouse (Okean Elzy album) |Lighthouse]]'' (2024)
* ''[[Toy den (Okean Elzy album) |Toy den]]'' (2024)
and also one live acoustic album ''[[Tviy format (Okean Elzy album)|Tviy format]]'' (Your Format, 2003).
